label: caiso 22 bidir+floor-only
definition: (PROBE — rejected, keeper stays caiso-import-cap-floor) Decomposition of the rejected caiso-21 unify: the single signed WECC bidir intertie (both legs at the measured hub) PLUS the RA gas-commitment floor 0.80, with NO per-tranche delivered-cost basis on the import legs (basis reverted in transmission.py inject_caiso_bidir_intertie_prices; the basis is the separate basis-only probe). Isolates whether the FLOOR alone is bidir-compatible. Run: --caiso-bidir-intertie --interchange-shaping --negative-renewable-offers --gas-hub-basis-overlay --priced-interchange --hydro-eia930-monthly --caiso-gas-commitment-floor, 3-yr. RESULT 2024: neg-price hrs 221 (keeper 815, actual ~800), net interchange -22.36 TWh (keeper -30.4, actual -32.4), p10 LMP $32.24 (keeper $1.40), mean $46.81 (keeper ~42, actual 35.8), diurnal corr +0.22. 2023: net -19.41 (actual -28.87), neg 48, mean 77.71, corr +0.95. 2025: net -30.63 (actual -36.16), neg 9, mean 52.01, corr +0.11. VERDICT: does NOT beat the keeper. Dropping the basis recovered some imports/tail vs the unify (2024 net -22.36 vs -17.68, neg 221 vs 194, corr +0.22 vs +0.09) — so the delivery basis WAS part of the import suppression — but the model STILL badly under-imports and the negative tail STILL collapses (221 vs keeper 815/actual ~800) and the body stays high. The bidir diurnal corr DOES survive the floor (positive every year: +0.95/+0.22/+0.11, vs the unify's +0.95/+0.09/-0.12), so the floor is diurnal-COMPATIBLE but level-ANTAGONISTIC: the RA gas floor forces gas online and suppresses imports / the negative tail on the single-flow node even with no basis. CONCLUSION: the FLOOR is (also) an import-suppressor on the bidir node — neither lever fully composes with bidir; basis was a secondary suppressor (confirm via the basis-only probe). Keeper unchanged. See results/calibration/NEXT-caiso-roadmap-2026-06-23.md.
